description: Decision journal of the historical ALNS + VND tuning on the development split (campaigns dev-001 ... dev-007, 2026-11-10). Text fields record the reasoning as it was stated during tuning; every number shown with this journal in main.ipynb is computed from the campaigns' run ledgers (runs.jsonl), never copied from here.
roles: The team set the goals (lowest gap to best-known solutions, CVRPTW scope, development/test discipline) and approved the protocol. Claude (Anthropic's AI assistant, working in Claude Code) proposed each hypothesis and the next configuration after reading the Python-computed results, and implemented the solver. Python executed every attempt (scripts/run_alns.py: isolated worker, hard wall-clock limit) and computed every number (scripts/benchmark.py: independent feasibility check, DIMACS scoring, gap to the published reference).
protocol: 36 development instances (one per size family x class), seeds 0 and 1, time limit max(10, 0.1 x customers) s per attempt, 6 concurrent workers. One setting changed at a time relative to the current best configuration. Decision rule used at the time: keep the change if the equal-weight mean gap over instances decreased, looking at how many instances improved versus worsened; the held-out test split was never used.

steps.change: Initial defaults from the literature: SA temperature 0.5 -> 0.01 x mean arc, 30 VND neighbours, all five destroy operators (random, worst, Shaw, string, route), q in [5, min(40, 0.2 n)]
steps.prompted_by: Starting point after implementation and profiling (a VND sweep dominated the iteration time).
steps.reasoning: All 72 attempts feasible and within budget. Two observations steered the next steps: about 70 % of candidate solutions were accepted, and worst removal ended with the lowest adaptive weight of the destroy operators.

steps.prompted_by: About 70 % acceptance in the baseline looked like too much random walk.
steps.hypothesis: A cooler schedule intensifies the search around good solutions and lowers the gap.
steps.reasoning: Worse overall and on most instances: accepting worse solutions was helping, so the next step tested the opposite direction.

steps.hypothesis: More diversification (accepting larger deteriorations early) escapes local optima better.
steps.reasoning: Lower mean gap than the baseline and better in five of six size families.

steps.hypothesis: Check whether the gains continue, to bracket the best temperature.
steps.reasoning: Worse than 1.5 -> 0.02 overall and on most instances, so 1.5 -> 0.02 was kept as the bracketed best of the values tried.

steps.change: VND examines 20 instead of 30 granular neighbours per customer
steps.prompted_by: Profiling showed that the VND takes almost all of an ALNS iteration.
steps.hypothesis: A narrower neighbourhood makes each iteration cheaper, so the same time budget buys more ALNS iterations, which matters most on large instances.
steps.reasoning: Slightly lower mean gap and more instances improved than worsened, with about 1.5x more iterations in the same time. The difference was small compared with seed noise; it was accepted on the point estimate plus the mechanism (speed).

steps.change: Remove at most 20 instead of 40 customers per ALNS iteration
steps.prompted_by: Smaller destroy steps are cheaper to repair and re-optimise.
steps.hypothesis: Smaller, more frequent changes improve the gap within the same budget.
steps.reasoning: No clear difference (about as many instances better as worse); the simpler choice was to keep the previous value 40.

steps.prompted_by: Worst removal had earned almost no adaptive weight: it finished with one of the two lowest destroy weights in every earlier campaign (the lowest in the baseline).
steps.hypothesis: The adaptive mechanism still spends some iterations on a weak operator; removing it frees those iterations for the useful ones.
steps.reasoning: Lower mean gap and more instances improved than worsened. As for step 5, the single-step difference was small relative to seed noise. This configuration was frozen and committed before any test instance was run.
